Beyond the owner's instruction, the read/search classification is relative to the identity running the script, so an answer computed under this context's identity would be confidently wrong rather than merely useless. Verified against synthetic trees instead.

prior_operator_result.what_it_localized: private-layout.json, its tmp sibling and every use-2 operand absent, so the run stopped before the layout save and before destination-home creation -- inside first inventory or subset selection. The five top directories are mode-permitted for the reported identity; their descendants were untested. use-1/home/.claude/projects is uid65532 gid1001 mode 0o2755.

probe_findings: A probe removing O_NOFOLLOW from directory opens PASSED at first: only the static source check noticed it, so nothing proved it mattered. test_a_symlinked_home_component_is_refused_not_walked was added -- the home's own path is where a following open would walk a decoy and report it as the home.

A probe reverting the scandir error handler PASSED, and taught me I had mislabelled my own test: mode 0600 on a directory is readable, so it opens and scandirs fine and the failure lands on the STAT handler, not opendir. The test was passing for a different reason than its name claimed. It was renamed and test_an_unopenable_directory_reports_an_opendir_error added for the mode 0000 case.

A wider-export-names probe was tried and REMOVED rather than counted: widening the export name list reverts nothing, because zip truncates against the six-element key, so a name can only leak if the key is widened too -- which names-in-the-export covers. Two independent changes are needed for a leak; that is a property of the code, not a gap in the tests.
selected: the review's second, conditional proposal: the bounded metadata-only home walk
